name: Pfrillsee Kufstein
kurzbeschreibung: Pfrillsee near Kufstein is the smallest and most secluded of Kufstein's forest lakes: a peaty natural gem, peaceful retreat, and water lily haven.
dauer: 1.5 to 3 hours (circular walk or quiet break)
preis: Lake area and circuit trail completely free of charge
beschreibung:
Overview

The mysterious and idyllic Pfrillsee lies at 615 meters elevation on the forested Thierberg hill above the fortress town of Kufstein, representing the smallest and most pristine of the four historic Kufstein woodland lakes. Tucked inside a protected forest hollow among beech trees, spruces, and reed beds, this protected body of water enchants visitors through absolute tranquil seclusion, dark peat-tinted waters, and undisturbed natural beauty. Unlike nearby Hechtsee, Pfrillsee features no commercial lidos, eateries, or road noise. The warm peat water reaches pleasant temperatures of up to 24 degrees Celsius in midsummer, making it a treasured local secret for a refreshing wild swim in absolute silence. The nutrient-rich moor lake supports rare water lilies, dragonflies, and native amphibians thriving along its shores.

Route & Requirements

Pfrillsee is reached exclusively on foot, preserving its undisturbed sanctuary character. The most popular access route is the scenic Four Lakes Hike, starting from the Hechtsee parking area and connecting Pfrillsee, Längsee, and Hechtsee in a family-friendly loop (total walking time approx. 2 hours, easy). Alternatively, a pleasant woodland path climbs from Kufstein-Zell over the Thierberg to the lake (approx. 45 minutes, 150 meters elevation gain). A narrow, natural forest trail circles the perimeter of Pfrillsee in about twenty minutes. Comfortable walking shoes or trainers with good traction are perfectly suitable for the forest paths. Due to occasional tree roots and short stepped sections, the perimeter path is not suitable for standard pushchairs or wheelchairs.

Visit & Arrival

The lake is open and freely accessible year-round without admission fees. Paid visitor parking is available at the Hechtsee lido, from where an easy 25-minute forest walk leads to Pfrillsee. Rail travelers arrive at Kufstein railway station with frequent long-distance and regional connections; local city buses head toward Zell and Hechtsee, with hiking trails clearly signposted.

Tips

Combine your lake visit with a short climb up to the nearby Thierberg castle ruins and historic hermitage: The panoramic viewing platform at the castle keep commands sweeping views over Kufstein, the Inn Valley, and the Kaiser mountains. Pack a picnic blanket to relax beneath shady forest canopies by the water.
saison: Ganzjährig frei zugänglich (Badesaison Juni bis September)
